chunk: The hallway stretched farther than it should have, fading into a darkness that seemed thicker with every step forward. Arjun paused at the entrance, trying to adjust his eyes, but the shadows resisted him. The air was colder inside, carrying

a faint smell of dust and something older, something forgotten. It felt as though the place had been untouched for years, yet not entirely abandoned. He moved slowly, each footstep deliberate, careful. The silence was unnatural. It was not the

quiet of an empty building, but something heavier, almost aware. His fingers brushed against the wall as he walked, tracing the uneven surface, grounding himself in something real. The texture was rough, colder than expected. Somewhere deeper in the hallway,

a faint sound emerged — not loud enough to be certain, but enough to unsettle him. He stopped instantly. His breath slowed, his ears straining to catch it again. For a moment, there was nothing. Just stillness. Then, just as

he convinced himself it had been nothing, the sound returned — softer this time, but closer. The shadows ahead seemed to shift slightly, though he could not be sure. He narrowed his eyes, focusing on the darkness, trying to find

a shape, a movement, anything that could explain what he felt. But the more he looked, the less certain he became. It was as if the darkness itself was absorbing detail, refusing to reveal anything clearly. A strange uneasiness settled

into his chest. Not fear, not yet — but something close. Something that told him he should not be there, that the hallway was not meant to be explored. And yet, he remained, standing between retreat and curiosity, unsure which

felt more dangerous. The air grew heavier as he moved forward again, each step slower than the last. The faint sound had stopped, but the silence it left behind felt even more unnatural. It pressed against him, as though it

were trying to fill the space completely, leaving no room for anything else. The hallway narrowed slightly, the walls closing in just enough to make him aware of the confinement. The darkness ahead deepened, turning from shadow into something almost

solid. He could no longer see the end of the corridor. It simply dissolved into black. He paused again, this time not because of a sound, but because of a feeling — a subtle shift in the air, as though

something had changed. The temperature dropped slightly, and a faint chill ran across his arms. He looked behind him instinctively. The entrance was still there, distant but visible, offering a way out. For a moment, he considered turning back. But

something held him in place. Not curiosity this time, but a quiet tension, as if leaving now would not change anything. As if whatever presence lingered here would follow, or worse, remain unnoticed until it was too late. He turned

forward again. The darkness ahead seemed to pulse faintly, not visibly, but in a way he could feel rather than see. His breathing became more measured, controlled, though his chest felt tight. The silence was no longer empty. It carried
weight. And then, just for a brief second, he felt it — not a sound, not a movement, but a certainty. Something was there. Not visible. Not moving. Just… present.
